newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia to sell off three more electric plants.
newsitem.headline: Colombia to sell off three more electric plants.

text.p: The Colombian government hopes to raise an additional $52.5 million in financing this year through the selloff of three small electrical power plants in the central and southwest part of the country, the state oil company Ecopetrol said.

It said the thermo-electric plants, with a combined capacity of 120 megawatts, were slated to be sold off in the second half of December and that the sale was to be handled by C.S. First Boston and Schroeders, Inverlink.
One of the plants is located in the industrial district of Yumbo on the outskirts of the southwest city of Cali, Ecopetrol said.
It said the other two were situated near Ibague, capital of central Tolima province, and on the outskirts of Villavicencio, capital of eastern Meta province.

The sale is in addition to that of four electric power plants, including the giant Chivor hydroelectric facility in central Boyaca province and the Betania hydroelectric plant in southwestern Huila, that the government announced in September.
Mines and Energy Minister Rodrigo Villamizar said the planned sale of the four plants should raise more than $1 billion. Chivor and Betania alone were valued at $990 million, he said.
